package_info.package_name: N/A (conceptual analysis, not a specific package)
package_info.why_malicious: The article does not analyze a specific malicious package, but rather draws an analogy between the inevitability and impact distribution of earthquakes and major open source software vulnerabilities/exploits. It highlights that, like earthquakes, a small number of high-impact open source vulnerabilities cause disproportionate damage, and that poor software supply chain hygiene makes organizations more susceptible to catastrophic breaches.

behavioral_signatures: Rapid exploitation attempts following public disclosure of a critical open source vulnerability
Automated scanning for newly disclosed vulnerabilities in widely used open source components
Mass probing of internet-facing applications for specific vulnerable endpoints (e.g., Struts CVE-2017-5638)
file_indicators: Presence of outdated or unpatched open source dependencies
Lack of automated dependency update or vulnerability management tooling
network_indicators: Unusual outbound traffic following vulnerability disclosure
Connections to known exploit command-and-control infrastructure after a new CVE is announced
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for rapid spikes in scanning or probing activity targeting newly disclosed vulnerabilities in open source components. Implement automated dependency and vulnerability management to ensure mean-time-to-remediation is minimized. Watch for signs of exploitation attempts (e.g., exploit payloads in logs) immediately following public vulnerability announcements. Correlate software bill of materials (SBOM) with threat intelligence to identify at-risk assets.
